results.title: UK: London's Santa School trains Father Christmas performers for 2026
results.content: Father Christmas is heading back to school in London. Professional Santas are learning sign language, brushing up on toy trends and preparing for the difficult questions children might ask this Christmas.

results.title: Iran's first women-only military training centre opens in Tehran
results.content: They will be trained by instructors with military experience in weapon use, firefighting, rescue, and civil assistance.

results.title: Daily life in Sudan paralysed by deepening fuel crisis and rising costs
results.content: Domestic refining has been crippled by the civil war while the Middle East conflict has led to significant fluctuations in oil prices.

results.title: Francophonie summit opens in Cambodia overshadowed by African tensions
results.content: The DR Congo objects to Rwanda's Louise Mushikiwabo seeking a third term as head of the organisation and threatens to quit if she is re-elected

results.title: Presidential polls open in Cape Verde with first female candidate
results.content: Incumbent Jose Maria Neves is favoured to win a second term in office in a country known for its stability in a politically volatile region.

results.title: Haitians welcome deployment of Salvadoran troops as gang violence rages on
results.content: The around 2,000 soldiers in Haiti are operating outside the official framework of the UN-back Gang Suppression Force.

results.title: Pope Leo denounces suffering of African enslaved people during Peru visit
results.content: He made the comment during a visit to the historic Afro-Peruvian city of Zaña, a UNESCO-recognised memorial site for slavery.

results.title: South Sudan postpones first general election from December to February
results.content: The elections commission says this will allow for the implementation of additional processes including distribution of registration materials and civic education.

results.title: DR Congo: Ebola-awareness campaigns conducted at schools in Bunia
results.content: About 40 schools in the province have reported cases of Ebola since classes resumed in September, with one teacher dying of the disease.

results.title: Microsoft apologises for global outage and rules out cyberattack
results.content: The tech giant said on Saturday that service has now been restored across Teams, Outlook, and its other products, ending the shutdown.

results.title: World Diabetes Day: South African health leaders urge early action to detect the disease
results.content: The health minister said the condition is now the country's number one killer, taking the top spot from HIV/AIDS.

results.title: Burkina Faso issues arrest warrants for around 20 people, including journalists
results.content: The warrants target exiled journalists, activists, an ex-minister, and former military officers who face several terrorism-related charges.

results.title: United States nationwide ground stop lifted after longest shutdown since 2001
results.content: The over four-hour stoppage on Friday brought all air travel to a halt across the country and stranded tens of thousands of passengers.

results.title: DR Congo: At least 44 dead in attack by Islamic State-linked gunmen
results.content: The latest raids by the Allied Democratic Forces come just days after the notoriously brutal group killed 66 people in North Kivu.

results.title: South Sudanese start registering to vote ahead of first national elections
results.content: The voter registration operation runs until 28 November ahead of the polls which have been postponed several times since independence in 2011.

results.title: France escalates Algeria trade dispute to EU-level
results.content: France on Friday asked the European Commission to look into Algeria’s alleged non-compliance with a EU trade deal. Paris is accusing Algers of an almost total blockade on French imports and of suspending urea shipments to France.

results.title: CAR: Opposition marches in Bangui against rising cost of living
results.content: Hundreds of people took to the streets of Bangui on Friday to protest the rising cost of living in Central African Republic and the arrest of five civil society leaders.

results.title: Burkinabe authorities vow to support gold miners expelled from Guinea
results.content: Since November 6, thousands of Burkinabe gold miners have been returning home. In Bobo-Dioulasso, more than 37,000 Burkinabe nationals, including some 8,000 children, as well as more than a thousand citizens of other nationalities, are hoping to start a new life with support from the authorities.

results.title: Teddy Riner announces presidential bid, pledges to unite France
results.content: In an interview with Le Parisien, Riner said he could not remain silent amid growing social tensions and uncertainty about France's future.

results.title: São Tomé's president reappoints PM following legislative elections
results.content: Américo Ramos' party came a close second in the polls, but the winning party, the Movement for the Liberation of São Tomé and Príncipe, failed to win additional support.

results.title: Cape verde presidential election: Neves seeks second term
results.content: The Portuguese-speaking island nation, located off the coast of Senegal, is widely regarded as one of Africa’s strongest democracies, standing out in a region increasingly affected by coups and political instability.

results.title: Nigeria Ebola patient contacts complete 21-day monitoring without signs of infection
results.content: Good news out of Nigeria where authorities say no further cases of Ebola have been detected since a woman arriving from Uganda tested positive for the virus last month.

results.title: DR Congo: Bukavu comedy festival offers laughter amid the ongoing conflict
results.content: For one week, comedians from the Republic of Congo, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, and the DRC offer residents a moment of relaxation and hope.

results.title: UK: Christmas at Kew 2026 unveils spectacular light trail in London
results.content: London's Kew Gardens has unveiled a dazzling Christmas light trail featuring more than a million lights and 24 installations. A spectacular new fountain and laser show takes centre stage.

results.title: North Macedonia: Kriva Palanka seeks help over 1,000 free-roaming cows
results.content: More than 1,000 cows are roaming freely through Kriva Palanka in North Macedonia, damaging property and alarming residents. The mayor wants the government to declare a 30-day state of crisis.

results.title: Turkey: Six-metre Trojan Horse spills plastic waste at COP31
results.content: A giant Trojan Horse overflowing with plastic waste has appeared in Antalya as Greenpeace International staged a striking environmental protest during the COP31 climate summit. Created with Danish artist Thomas Dambo, the Greenpeace installation warns of the environmental impact of plastics.

results.title: Burundi: 11 opposition parties announce support for President Ndayishimiye's re-election bid
results.content: Burundi’s President Evariste Ndayishimiye has secured the backing of 11 opposition parties when he runs for re-election next year.

results.title: Kenyans brace for El Niño rains as flood survivors fear a repeat of 2024 devastation
results.content: The warning comes as Nairobi continues to grapple with urban planning challenges, encroachment on wetlands and construction in flood-prone areas, factors that increase the city's vulnerability to flooding.

results.title: New witness due in former South African minister's corruption trial
results.content: Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula faces 12 counts of corruption and one of money laundering, stemming from her time as defence minister.

results.title: Swiss hospital discharges Ebola patient after successful treatment
results.content: A Swiss woman who contracted the strain of Ebola linked to the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been discharged from hospital in Geneva, health officials said on Thursday.
